companyDescription: Launch + space systems · Electron/HASTE operational, Neutron debut targeted Q4 2026 · pending $8B Iridium acquisition (closing ~mid-2027) · Q2 2026 earnings land AFTER CLOSE today, Aug 10
priceNote: ⚠️ This snapshot is PRE-RESULTS — Q2 2026 earnings report after market close today (Aug 10), with the call at 5:00pm ET. Stock is up 2.96% today and has run 45.5% in under two weeks, from a $58.60 close on Jul 29 to $85.30 now, fueled by a run of Space Force contract wins. Still 43.5% below the May 27 all-time-high close of $151.00.
summary: Rocket Lab reports Q2 2026 results after the close TODAY (Aug 10) — this snapshot is written ahead of that print. The setup is genuinely two-sided: the stock has run 45.5% in under two weeks (from $58.60 on Jul 29 to $85.30) on a run of real contract wins — the $266M Space Force HASTE deal (Jul 27) and a new $397M Space Force SB-AMTI 'Flatellite' satellite-tracking award (Aug 4, notably tied to the still-undelivered Neutron rocket) — plus a fresh KGI Securities upgrade to Outperform ($107 target). Consensus sees $231.6M revenue (+60.3% YoY) and an EPS loss of -$0.06. RKLB's own history shows a good print isn't automatically enough: a clean Q1 2026 beat sent shares +34%, but a Q4 2025 beat still dropped -9.5% days later purely on Neutron-timeline news — and this time the bar is set even higher after a 45% pre-earnings run.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings — REPORTS TODAY AFTER CLOSE
catalysts.description: Reports after market close today, Aug 10, 2026, call at 5:00pm ET. Consensus: $231.6M revenue (+60.3% YoY), EPS -$0.06 (improved from -$0.13 a year ago). After a 45.5% pre-earnings run, both the headline numbers AND any Neutron-timeline commentary will move the stock — RKLB has a real history of a clean beat still selling off on guidance/roadmap nuance.

catalysts.name: Neutron First Launch
catalysts.description: Medium-lift, partially reusable rocket — delayed twice, most recently to Q4 2026 after a January 2026 hydrostatic tank-test failure. The Aug 4 $397M Space Force contract is explicitly tied to Neutron, raising the stakes on a clean debut; a third slip would hit sentiment hard given how much is now priced in.

catalysts.name: Space Force Contract Momentum
catalysts.description: Two large wins in 10 days: the $266M HASTE suborbital contract (Jul 27, RKLB's largest-ever at the time) and a new $397M SB-AMTI 'Flatellite' satellite-tracking award (Aug 4) that will fly on Neutron. Backlog keeps growing outside the earnings calendar.

catalysts.name: Iridium Acquisition ($8B)
catalysts.description: Announced Jun 29, 2026 — cash-and-stock deal to acquire Iridium Communications, creating a vertically integrated launch-plus-constellation operator. Expected to close mid-2027 pending approvals.

risks: Earnings reactions cut both ways for this exact stock — a clean Q1 2026 beat sent RKLB +34%, but a Q4 2025 beat still triggered a -9.5% drop days later purely on Neutron-timeline news; after a 45.5% pre-earnings run into tonight's print, the bar for 'good enough' is higher than ever

Neutron has now slipped twice (originally early 2026, then Q1, now Q4 2026) — a real, repeatable pattern risk, and the new $397M SB-AMTI contract is explicitly tied to it, raising the cost of a third delay
Rich, pre-profit valuation — market cap has grown to ~$51B on a stock still guided to a net loss this quarter (EPS -$0.06 est.)

Extreme high-beta/sentiment-driven — the stock round-tripped roughly -61% then +45% within about a month on a mix of sector-wide and company-specific factors, showing how disconnected price action can be from any single data point
Iridium deal adds integration and dilution risk — $8B cash+stock transaction, new share issuance, and a long ~mid-2027 close mean execution risk stacks on top of the core launch business
